(a) All contracts involving the use of appropriated funds which shall hereafter be entered into by any department or agency of the executive branch for performance in any State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, or the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands shall, unless otherwise provided by law, contain a stipulation forbidding in the performance of such contracts, the employment of persons undergoing sentences of imprisonment which have been imposed by any court of a State. the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, or the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands.

THE PRESIDENT 10069
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11713
D elegating C ertain Functions Vested in the President to the  
Adm inistrator o f General Services
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 301 of title 3 of 
the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
hereby ordered as follows:
S e c t i o n 1. Section 1  of Executive Order No. 11609 of July 22, 1971, 
is hereby amended by adding at the end thereof the following new 
paragraphs:
“ (22) The authority of the President under section 372 of title 2 of 
the Canal Zone Code to approve transfers between departments and 
agencies of certain property in the Canal Zone.
“ (23) The authority of the President under section 62(d)  of title 2 
of the Canal Zone Code to approve the valuation of properties and other 
assets being transferred between the Panama Canal Company and other 
Government agencies.”
S e c. 2. All actions heretofore taken by the President, the Director of 
the Bureau of the Budget, or the Director of the Office of Management 
and Budget in respect of matters affected by the amendment made by 
section 1  of this order and in force at the time of the issuance of this 
order, including any regulations prescribed or approved by any of them 
in respect of such matters, shall, except as may be inconsistent with the 
provisions of this order, remain in effect until amended, modified, or 
revoked pursuant to the authority conferred by this order unless sooner 
terminated by operation of law.
Sec. 3. Executive Order No. 11541 of July 1, 1970, is superseded to 
the extent that it is inconsistent with this order.
T h e W h i t e H o u s e,
April 21, 1973.
[FR D oc.73-8054 Filed 4 -2 3 -7 3 ;1 0 :13 am]
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 38, N O . 78— TUESDAY, APRIL 24, 1973

35 FR 11161, Federal Register issue of July 11, 1970) establishes the Defense Distinguished Service Medal. I read the complete held Federal Register text (a machine text layer of the printed page): an authority paragraph and four sections (establishment and eligibility; design, regulations and precedence; one medal with devices; posthumous award). The held text has a few dropped words in section 4 and a misspelled title, so I quote nothing from those lines. The dossier inventory is one clause covering the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition and revokes nothing. EO 14085 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541), section 6, amends it: section 1 is amended by striking military officer and inserting member of the Armed Forces of the United States, and section 2 by striking he and inserting the Secretary. That is a later event on a continuing clause, recorded with its text before and after in the clause reason, not an end. The held-text number search also finds only the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (historical editorial, not a current basis) and EO 14085. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1125 with no ending statement (a machine pointer; held statutory text is not relied on). The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record only the EO 14085 amendment and no revocation or supersession. Every command is a standing duty of federal agencies or the Secretary of the Interior. The dated paragraphs, 2(a) (by July 1, 1973) and 2(e) (by January 1, 1972 and annually thereafter), are deadlines, not ends, and paragraph 2(b) is applied today: the held current 36 CFR 63.1 says the Interior regulations explain determinations of eligibility under section 2(b) of the order and implement sections 1(3) and 2(b), and 36 CFR parts 60, 63 and 68 and many other eCFR parts name the order as of 2026-10-14. No later instrument amending, revoking or superseding it is held (the chain is empty; EO 13006 and EO 13022 recite it without changing it). Section 2 is amended to read: \"The Export Control Review Board established by Section 2 of Executive Order No. 10945 of May 24, 1961, is hereby re-established as the Export Administration Review Board, hereinafter referred to as the Board.  The Board shall be composed of the Secretary of Commerce, who shall be Chairman of the Board, the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, and the Chairman of the East-West Foreign Trade Board (Section 7 of Executive Order No. 11846, as amended). No alternative Board members shall he designated, but the acting head of any department may serve in lieu of the head of the department concerned. In the case of the East-West Foreign Trade Board, the Deputy Chairman may serve in lieu of the Chairman. The Board may invite the heads of other Government organizations and agencies to participate in the activities of the Board when matters of interest to such organizations and agencies are under consideration.\".\n\nGERALD R. Section 1 authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, to implement an agreement concluded in December 1974 with the Commission of the European Communities by issuing regulations (a) preventing importation into the Customs Territory of the United States, except Puerto Rico, of certain European Communities cheeses on which restitution payments have been made for export to Puerto Rico, other possessions or any country other than the United States, and (b) preventing importation of such cheeses into Puerto Rico for transshipment elsewhere in the Customs Territory. Section 2 authorizes heads of departments and agencies to redelegate, with the Treasury regulation-issuing function redelegable only to officials appointed by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, as 3 U.S.C. 301 provides. The packet's machine inventory merged section 2 into subsection (b) and left a fragment '301.' as a fourth clause, so I corrected the inventory into four clauses with absolute character spans in the held original text (section 1 lead-in and recital, subsection (a), subsection (b), section 2). Search of held texts for the number EO 11851 finds only the order, the 1989 OFR codification (no amendment or revocation) and 19 CFR 12.6; the OFR catalog record has no disposition note; the bounded searches report no machine hit that ends or amends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The held text of 19 CFR 12.6 (eCFR searched point-in-time as of 2026-10-14) names the order. The order's own text states no end date, event or condition; the December 1974 agreement is its purpose, not a condition of its continuance, and no held source shows that agreement ended. All four clauses are operative as of 2026-10-14.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"The order states no end date, event or condition; held texts naming EO 11851 (the order, the 1989 codification and 19 CFR 12.6) record no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment, and the OFR catalog has no disposition note.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"Subsections (a) and (b) are separate EO 11884 (signed 1975-10-07; 40 FR 47469; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11884.txt, read in full) prescribes the official Coat of Arms, Seal and Color and Flag of the Vice President of the United States and revokes Executive Order No. 10016. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11884 of October 7, 1975, prescribing the official coat of arms, seal and flag of the Vice President at 40 FR 47469, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has one clause for the whole operative text, so I replaced it with five clauses (inventory override): sections 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5; section 5 is the effective-date and revocation section. Own terms: sections 1 to 4 have no end date or ending condition; section 5 is a self-executing effective-date and revocation provision performed on issuance, recorded as terminated on 1975-10-07. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11884 finds only the 1989 codification snapshot (and the order's own Federal Register copy); the dossier chain has no event and lists no actor. No held text revokes, supersedes or amends the order. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 0, 0 and 0 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate for sections 1 to 4 rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the attached illustrations and specifications at 40 FR 47470 are image pages whose graphic content is not read here.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"Sections 1 to 4 have no own-terms end, and no held order text, statute text or search result revokes, supersedes or amends EO 11884.
